answer: At an oasis herb exchange, agents earn fees for arranging yarrow deliveries. Each buyer signs a receipt tied to a unique order ID; the contract pays that order once and treats copies as an echo, regardless of seller account. To claim more fees, an attacker must finance separate real deliveries and lock a bond that can be slashed if audits find no goods. Colluding buyers can still sign phantom receipts, so random inventory checks and delayed settlement reduce the risk, though bonds may exclude small honest traders.
